topic: Doer vs Receiver Focus, Transformation, Tenses, Pronouns, SVOO & Limits

situationBrief.title: Active and Passive Voice
situationBrief.description: Learn how Active Voice spotlights the doer, how Passive Voice shifts focus to the receiver with be + Past Participle, and when Passive works naturally.

grammarOutcomes: Distinguish Active Voice (Subject = doer) from Passive Voice (Subject = receiver) while keeping event meaning and time unchanged.
Convert transitive clauses accurately using New Subject + matching be auxiliary + Past Participle (V-en / V3) across tenses, aspects, modals, pronouns, SVOO, questions, and imperatives.
Decide when to omit 'by + doer', recognise non-passivisable intransitive and linking clauses, and spot common Voice errors.
learningObjectives.knowledgeOutcome: Explore Indian school gardens, ISRO weather science, heritage monuments, and everyday healthy food habits through clear interactive Voice patterns.

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Active (Doer Focus)
sentences.rawText: Mira waters the mango saplings.
sentences.note: In Active Voice, the Subject 'Mira' is the doer performing the action 'waters'.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Names the person doing the watering.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Subject head-noun and doer (agent) in Active Voice.
Singular present verb agreeing with 'Mira' and passing action to 'saplings'.
Direct Object head-noun receiving the action.

groups.label: Subject (Doer)
groups.plainExplanation: 'Mira' is the Subject and the doer of the watering action.
groups.textbookRule: In Active Voice, the grammatical Subject is the doer (agent) of the verb.

groups.label: Predicate (Action + Receiver)
groups.plainExplanation: 'waters the mango saplings' states the action and its receiver ('the mango saplings').
groups.textbookRule: Transitive active verbs pass their action onto a Direct Object.

structureSummary.patternNote: Active SVO: Mira (Doer / Subject) + waters (Action) + the mango saplings (Receiver / Object).

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Passive (Receiver Focus)
sentences.rawText: The mango saplings are watered by Mira.
sentences.note: Now 'The mango saplings' (receiver) sits in the Subject spotlight! Notice the event and present time did not change.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Former Object promoted to Subject; plural 'saplings' requires plural 'are'.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Keeps present time and matches plural 'saplings'.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Finite 'be' auxiliary carrying Present tense + plural agreement.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Names the action received by the saplings.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Past participle paired with 'are' to form Passive Voice.
Links the optional doer ('Mira') to the passive verb.
Original doer placed inside an optional 'by'-phrase.

groups.label: Subject (Receiver)
groups.plainExplanation: 'The mango saplings' is now the Subject—it receives the action instead of doing it.
groups.textbookRule: In Passive Voice, the receiver of the action becomes the grammatical Subject.

groups.label: Predicate (be + V-en + by-phrase)
groups.questionPrompt: What is done to the Subject?
groups.plainExplanation: 'are watered by Mira' uses present plural 'are' + past participle 'watered' + optional doer 'by Mira'.
groups.textbookRule: Passive Voice pairs a form of 'be' with the Past Participle (V-en / V3).

structureSummary.patternNote: Passive: The mango saplings (Receiver / Subject) + are watered (be + V-en) + by Mira (Doer).

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Present Habit Passive
sentences.rawText: Fresh guavas are packed in bamboo baskets.
sentences.note: Even though 'packed' ends in -ed, helper 'are' tells us this is a regular Present-time habit.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Shows Present time and plural agreement.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Present-tense 'be' proves this passive sentence is NOT past tense.
Starts the place phrase 'in bamboo baskets'.

groups.label: Subject (Receiver)
groups.plainExplanation: 'Fresh guavas' sits in the Subject slot and receives the action of packing.
groups.textbookRule: A Past Participle (-ed/-en) in Passive Voice does not mean Past time; the 'be' helper sets time.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.questionPrompt: What is done to the guavas?
groups.plainExplanation: 'are packed in bamboo baskets' uses present 'are' + 'packed' to describe a present routine.
groups.textbookRule: Use am/is/are + Past Participle for Present Simple Passive.

structureSummary.patternNote: Present Passive: Fresh guavas (Receiver) + are (Present be) + packed (V-en) + place phrase.

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Past Time Passive
sentences.rawText: Fresh guavas were packed in bamboo baskets yesterday.
sentences.note: Only 'are' switched to 'were' (+ 'yesterday') to show Past time; 'packed' stayed identical!

tokens.meaningInSentence: Shifts the Passive sentence to Past time.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Past plural form of 'be' agreeing with 'guavas'.
Unchanged past participle; time comes from 'were'.

groups.label: Subject (Receiver)
groups.plainExplanation: 'Fresh guavas' remains the receiver Subject.
groups.textbookRule: Past Simple Passive uses was/were + Past Participle.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.questionPrompt: What changed to show Past time?
groups.plainExplanation: 'were' replaced 'are' to mark Past time, while 'packed' stayed the same.
groups.textbookRule: In Passive Voice, the 'be' auxiliary—never the Past Participle—shows tense.

structureSummary.predicateText: were packed in bamboo baskets yesterday.
structureSummary.patternNote: Past Passive: Fresh guavas (Receiver) + were (Past be) + packed (V-en) + yesterday.

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Active SVO
sentences.rawText: The chef washes fresh vegetables.
sentences.note: Ask 'washes what?' -> 'fresh vegetables' (Direct Object). Having an Object makes Passive transformation possible!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Singular Present Simple verb agreeing with 'chef'.
Plural Direct Object ready to move to Subject spot in Passive.

groups.label: Subject (Doer)
groups.plainExplanation: 'The chef' is the singular doer in the Subject slot.
groups.textbookRule: Identify Subject, Finite Verb, and Direct Object before shifting Voice.

groups.label: Predicate (Verb + Object)
groups.plainExplanation: 'washes' (Verb) + 'fresh vegetables' (Direct Object answering 'washes what?').
groups.textbookRule: Only transitive clauses with an Object can move that Object into Passive Subject position.

structureSummary.patternNote: Active SVO: The chef (S) + washes (V) + fresh vegetables (O).

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · 4-Step Passive Shift
sentences.rawText: Fresh vegetables are washed by the chef.
sentences.note: Watch 'washes' (singular for 'chef') turn into 'are washed' (plural for 'Fresh vegetables')!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Moved with 'vegetables' as one noun group.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Former Object now leading the sentence.
Keeps Present time and agrees with plural 'vegetables'.

groups.label: New Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'Fresh vegetables' moved from Object to Subject.
groups.textbookRule: Step 1: Move the complete Object noun group to Subject position.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: 'are' (present + plural) + 'washed' (Past Participle) + 'by the chef'.
groups.textbookRule: Steps 2-4: Add matching 'be', lock main verb to V-en, and add 'by + doer' if needed.

structureSummary.patternNote: 4-Step Passive: New S (Fresh vegetables) + be (are) + V-en (washed) + by-phrase.

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Irregular Participle & New Agreement
sentences.rawText: Two science notes were written by Arjun.
sentences.note: Plural new Subject 'Two science notes' needs plural 'were', and irregular 'wrote' (V2) must become 'written' (V-en / V3).

tokens.meaningInSentence: Tells the topic of the notes.
Marks Past time and plural Subject.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Past participle of 'write' (never use V2 'wrote' after 'were').

groups.label: New Plural Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'Two science notes' is plural, so it requires 'were' (not 'was').
groups.textbookRule: The passive auxiliary 'be' always agrees with the new Subject, never the old doer.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: 'were written' pairs plural past 'were' with Past Participle 'written' (V-en / V3).
groups.textbookRule: Never use Past Simple V2 ('wrote, sang, broke') after 'be'; use Past Participle V-en ('written, sung, broken').

structureSummary.patternNote: Agreement + Irregular V-en: Plural Subject (notes) -> were + Past Participle (written).

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Active Past (V2)
sentences.rawText: Arjun wrote two science notes.
sentences.note: In Active Past, 'wrote' is Simple Past (V2) and agrees with singular 'Arjun'. Watch how Passive upgrades V2 to 'were written'!

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'Arjun' is the singular Subject doer.
groups.textbookRule: Active Past uses V2 directly.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.questionPrompt: What is the verb and object?
groups.plainExplanation: 'wrote' (V2) + plural Object 'two science notes'.
groups.textbookRule: V2 changes to was/were + V-en in Passive.

structureSummary.patternNote: Active Past: Arjun (S) + wrote (V2) + two science notes (plural O).

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Progressive Passive
sentences.rawText: A solar chart is being painted right now.
sentences.note: To keep an action ongoing ('right now'), insert 'being' between 'is' and 'painted'!

tokens.meaningInSentence: Shows the painting is in progress right now.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Part of the time clue 'right now'.

groups.label: Subject (Receiver)
groups.plainExplanation: 'A solar chart' is singular and receives the ongoing action.
groups.textbookRule: Singular Subject takes 'is' or 'was' at the front of the Progressive passive chain.

groups.label: Predicate (is being painted)
groups.plainExplanation: 'is' (tense/agreement) + 'being' (ongoing -ing) + 'painted' (V-en).
groups.textbookRule: Progressive / Continuous Passive follows am/is/are/was/were + being + Past Participle.

structureSummary.patternNote: Progressive Passive: is (Present) + being (Ongoing) + painted (V-en).

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Progressive Active
sentences.rawText: The students are painting a solar chart right now.
sentences.note: Active 'are painting' switches agreement to singular 'is' and keeps the -ing aspect via 'being' -> 'is being painted'.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'The students' (plural doer Subject).
groups.textbookRule: Plural Subject takes 'are'.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: 'are painting a solar chart right now'.
groups.textbookRule: Active -ing transfers into Passive 'being + V-en'.

structureSummary.predicateText: are painting a solar chart right now.
structureSummary.patternNote: Active Progressive: are painting -> Passive: is being painted.

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Perfect Passive
sentences.rawText: The weather satellite has been launched by ISRO.
sentences.note: In Perfect Passive, 'has/have/had' stays at the front and 'been' steps in right before Past Participle 'launched'.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Shows completed action linked to present.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Main verb in Past Participle form.
Specific informative agent kept in the 'by'-phrase.

groups.label: Subject (Receiver)
groups.plainExplanation: 'The weather satellite' is singular and receives the action.
groups.textbookRule: Perfect Passive keeps 'has / have / had' matched to the new Subject.

groups.label: Predicate (has been launched)
groups.questionPrompt: What makes the Perfect verb passive?
groups.plainExplanation: 'been' sits between 'has' and 'launched'—without 'been', 'has launched' would be Active!
groups.textbookRule: Perfect Passive = has/have/had + been + Past Participle.

structureSummary.patternNote: Perfect Passive: has (Perfect) + been (Passive be) + launched (V-en).

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Modal Passive
sentences.rawText: Clean shoes must be worn by every runner.
sentences.note: Modals ('can, may, must, should') and 'will' always take bare base 'be' + Past Participle!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Modal helper stays unchanged before base 'be'.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'Clean shoes' receives the rule.
groups.textbookRule: Modal Passive keeps the modal intact.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.questionPrompt: How does a modal form Passive?
groups.plainExplanation: 'must + be + worn' (Modal + bare 'be' + Past Participle).
groups.textbookRule: Future 'will' and modals ('can, may, must, should') always take bare 'be' + V-en.

structureSummary.predicateText: must be worn by every runner.
structureSummary.patternNote: Modal Passive: Modal (must) + base be + Past Participle (worn).

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Pronoun Case Swap
sentences.rawText: They were praised by her.
sentences.note: In Active 'She praised them', crossing the verb swaps case: Object 'them' -> Subject 'They', and Subject 'She' -> Object 'her' after 'by'!

tokens.meaningInSentence: Refers to the receivers of the praise.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Object pronoun 'them' changed to Subject case 'They'.
Any pronoun after a preposition must be Object case.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Refers to the person who gave the praise.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Subject pronoun 'She' changed to Object case 'her' after 'by'.

groups.label: Subject Pronoun
groups.questionPrompt: Who sits in the Subject slot?
groups.plainExplanation: 'They' (Subject case, converted from Object 'them').
groups.textbookRule: Use Subject-case pronouns (I, we, he, she, they) in Subject position.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: 'were praised by her' uses Object-case 'her' (never 'by she').
groups.textbookRule: Use Object-case pronouns (me, us, him, her, them, whom) after 'by'.

structureSummary.patternNote: Pronoun Swap: They (Subject case) + were praised + by her (Object case).

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Active Pronouns
sentences.rawText: She praised them.
sentences.note: Here 'She' is in the Subject slot and 'them' is in the Object slot. Swapping Voice flips their cases too!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Subject case 'She' becomes 'by her' in Passive.
Object case 'them' becomes 'They' in Passive Subject spot.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'She' (Subject case).
groups.textbookRule: Pronouns change form when moving between Subject and Object slots.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: 'praised them' ('them' = Object case).
groups.textbookRule: Object 'them' becomes Subject 'They' when passivised.

structureSummary.patternNote: Active Pronouns: She (Subject) + praised + them (Object).

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Two Objects (SVOO)
sentences.rawText: Mira was given a certificate by the coach.
sentences.note: From 'The coach gave Mira (IO) a certificate (DO)': promoting recipient 'Mira' gives the cleanest Passive!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Indirect Object ('Mira') moved to Subject spot.

tokens.meaningInSentence: Names what was handed to Mira.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Second Object kept after the passive verb.

groups.label: Subject (Recipient)
groups.questionPrompt: Which of the two Objects became Subject?
groups.plainExplanation: The person receiving ('Mira', the Indirect Object) became Subject; alternatively, 'A certificate was given to Mira...'.
groups.textbookRule: SVOO verbs ('give, send, lend, teach') allow either Object to become Passive Subject.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.questionPrompt: What remains after the passive verb?
groups.plainExplanation: 'was given' + retained Direct Object 'a certificate' + 'by the coach'.
groups.textbookRule: If you promote the Direct Object ('A certificate') instead, insert 'to' or 'for' before the recipient.

structureSummary.predicateText: was given a certificate by the coach.
structureSummary.patternNote: SVOO Passive: Mira (IO -> S) + was given + a certificate (Retained DO) + by the coach.

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Question Passive
sentences.rawText: Was the courtyard cleaned by the students?
sentences.note: From 'Did the students clean the courtyard?': replace 'Did' with 'Was' and place 'Was' BEFORE the new Subject!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Replaces 'Did' and stands before Subject 'the courtyard'.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'the courtyard' sits between auxiliary 'Was' and participle 'cleaned' to form a question.
groups.textbookRule: Passive questions keep Auxiliary + New Subject + Past Participle order.

groups.label: Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: 'Was ... cleaned by the students?' drops 'Did' and uses past 'be' ('Was').
groups.textbookRule: Never use 'do / does / did' inside Passive Voice questions.

structureSummary.patternNote: Passive Question: Was (Inverted be) + the courtyard (New S) + cleaned (V-en)?

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Omitting Vague 'by'
sentences.rawText: The library steps were swept before dawn.
sentences.note: From 'Someone swept the library steps before dawn'—dropping 'by someone' makes the Passive sentence crisp and natural!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: No 'by someone' needed; ends smoothly with time phrase 'before dawn'.

groups.label: Subject (Result Focus)
groups.questionPrompt: Why does the sentence start with 'The library steps'?
groups.plainExplanation: The visible result on the steps matters more than knowing which unknown 'someone' swept them.
groups.textbookRule: Omit 'by + doer' when the doer is unknown, general ('people, someone, they'), or obvious.

groups.label: Agentless Passive Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: No! Agentless passives ('were swept before dawn') are standard, concise English.
groups.textbookRule: Most real-world Passive sentences in science, news, and notices omit 'by + agent'.

structureSummary.patternNote: Natural Agentless Passive: The library steps + were swept + before dawn (no 'by someone').

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Tool ('with') vs Doer ('by')
sentences.rawText: The ripe mangoes were sliced with a clean knife by the cook.
sentences.note: People take 'by' ('by the cook'), while physical tools take 'with' ('with a clean knife')—never 'by a knife'!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Always use 'with' (not 'by') before a tool like 'a clean knife'.
Use 'by' for the person performing the action.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'The ripe mangoes' (Receiver Subject).
groups.textbookRule: Keep human agent ('by') distinct from physical tool ('with').

groups.label: Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: 'with a clean knife' marks the tool; 'by the cook' marks the person.
groups.textbookRule: Use 'by' for the doer and 'with' for the instrument.

structureSummary.predicateText: were sliced with a clean knife by the cook.
structureSummary.patternNote: with (Tool: clean knife) vs by (Doer: the cook).

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Intransitive (No Object)
sentences.rawText: The school train arrived at six.
sentences.note: Ask 'arrived what?' -> No answer! 'at six' tells WHEN (Adverbial), not an Object—so this sentence CANNOT become Passive.

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Intransitive verb: cannot take an Object or Passive form.
Opens an Adverbial of Time (NOT an Object).
Part of Adverbial 'at six'; cannot become a Passive Subject.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'The school train' is the Subject, and there is no receiver.
groups.textbookRule: Intransitive verbs (arrive, sleep, happen, sit, go) take no Object.

groups.label: Predicate (Intransitive SVA)
groups.plainExplanation: No! 'at six' tells when (Adverbial), not what was acted on—so no Passive exists.
groups.textbookRule: Without a Direct Object, a clause cannot be converted to Passive Voice.

structureSummary.patternNote: Cannot Be Passive (SVA): arrived (Intransitive V) + at six (Time Adverbial, NOT Object).

sentences.title: Compare Sentence · Linking Verb (SVC)
sentences.rawText: The morning breeze felt cool and fresh.
sentences.note: 'cool and fresh' describes 'The morning breeze' (Subject Complement), NOT a separate Object—so no Passive exists!

tokens.meaningInSentence: Connects the Subject to its quality.
tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Linking verb (breeze = cool and fresh), NOT a transitive action here.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: 'The morning breeze' = 'cool and fresh'.
groups.textbookRule: Linking verbs ('be, become, seem, feel, taste') join Subject to Complement (SVC).

groups.label: Predicate (Linking SVC)
groups.plainExplanation: 'cool and fresh' describes the Subject rather than naming a separate receiver Object.
groups.textbookRule: SVC linking clauses and state verbs ('have, belong, resemble') cannot become Passive.

structureSummary.patternNote: Cannot Be Passive (SVC): Linking verb 'felt' connects breeze = cool and fresh (no Object).

sentences.title: Starter Sentence · Repaired 5-Point Passive
sentences.rawText: The science posters were drawn by them before assembly.
sentences.note: Fixed from 'was drew by they': plural 'were' matches 'posters', V-en 'drawn' replaces V2 'drew', and 'them' replaces 'they'!

tokens.grammaticalRoleExplanation: Repairs Subject pronoun 'they' to Object pronoun 'them'.

groups.label: Subject
groups.plainExplanation: Plural 'The science posters' locks onto plural 'were'.
groups.textbookRule: Check Subject number, 'be' form, Past Participle, and Pronoun case together.

groups.label: Repaired Predicate
groups.plainExplanation: 'were' (plural agreement), 'drawn' (V-en participle), and 'them' (Object pronoun after 'by').
groups.textbookRule: Apply the 5-Point Voice Check to repair any broken Passive sentence.

structureSummary.predicateText: were drawn by them before assembly.
structureSummary.patternNote: 3-Fix Audit: posters (plural) -> were + drawn (V-en) + by them (Object case).

teachingSequence.title: What Voice Means: Doer Focus vs Receiver Focus
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Voice chooses who sits in the Subject spotlight: the doer (Active) or the receiver (Passive)—without changing the real event.
teachingSequence.explanation: Compare Active 'Mira waters the mango saplings' with Passive 'The mango saplings are watered by Mira'. In Active Voice, the doer leads; in Passive Voice, the receiver leads.

clausePatternData.categoryBadge: Topic 1 · Two Views of One Event
clausePatternData.whyItWorks: Both sentences describe the exact same morning garden scene. Active Voice puts the doer ('Mira') first; Passive Voice moves the receiver ('The mango saplings') to the front because we want to talk about the saplings.
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Active puts the doer in the Subject slot; Passive moves the receiver into the Subject slot.

keyTerms.meaning: The grammatical Subject performs the action (e.g., 'Mira waters the mango saplings').
The grammatical Subject receives the action (e.g., 'The mango saplings are watered by Mira').

segments.label: Passive Voice
segments.text: The mango saplings are watered by Mira.

relationDiagram.caption: Changing Voice shifts spotlight from doer to receiver while keeping the meaning and time intact.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Arjun carries the water can. -> The water can is carried by Arjun.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Active Subject 'Arjun' does the carrying. 2) Passive moves receiver 'The water can' to the Subject spot.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Both describe Arjun carrying the can right now.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Our school cooks prepare warm millet porridge. -> Warm millet porridge is prepared by our school cooks.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Active focuses on the cooks. 2) Passive spotlights the healthy meal ('Warm millet porridge').
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Switching Subject changes emphasis, not facts.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Bees pollinate orchard flowers in spring. -> Orchard flowers are pollinated by bees in spring.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Identify doer ('Bees') and receiver ('Orchard flowers'). 2) Notice time phrase 'in spring' stays at the end.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Passive lets a nature report stay focused on 'Orchard flowers'.

commonMistake.incorrectText: Thinking the first noun (Subject) is always the person doing the action.
commonMistake.correctText: Check the verb ('are watered') to see whether the Subject acts or receives the action.
commonMistake.whyWrong: In Passive Voice, the Subject is the receiver, while the doer is pushed after 'by' or omitted.

boardNote.label: Grammar Note · Subject Spotlight Test
boardNote.text: To tell Active from Passive fast, ask: 'Did the Subject DO this verb or RECEIVE it?' If it received the action and uses be + Past Participle, it is Passive.

teachingSequence.title: Same Time in Voice: Clearing the Past-Time Myth
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Passive Voice does NOT automatically mean Past time! Look at 'be' ('are' vs 'were') to read the time.
teachingSequence.explanation: Because Passive Voice uses Past Participle forms like 'packed' or 'grown', learners often think every Passive sentence is in the Past. Actually, the 'be' helper sets the time!

clausePatternData.whyItWorks: In 'are packed' and 'were packed', the Past Participle 'packed' never changes for time. The finite 'be' verb ('are' = Present, 'were' = Past) tells you when the action happens.
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Passive Voice keeps the original time; check 'be' (am/is/are vs was/were) for tense, not the -ed/-en ending.

keyTerms.meaning: Uses am / is / are + Past Participle for present habits, facts, and routines.
Uses was / were + Past Participle for completed past events.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Millet is grown in dry farms.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Find helper 'is' -> Present time. 2) 'grown' is the Past Participle.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Present helper 'is' shows an ongoing agricultural fact today.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Fifty saplings were planted last Sunday.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Find helper 'were' -> Past time matching 'last Sunday'. 2) 'planted' completes the Passive verb.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: 'were' matches both Past time and plural 'saplings'.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Fresh rice is harvested in autumn, and yesterday's harvest was stored cleanly.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) 'is harvested' states a general rule (Present). 2) 'was stored' reports yesterday's event (Past).
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Both use -ed/-en participles, yet 'is' vs 'was' cleanly separates Present from Past.

commonMistake.incorrectText: Thinking 'Fresh rice is grown in our valley' happened in the past because 'grown' is a past participle.
commonMistake.correctText: Helper 'is' + 'grown' = Present Simple Passive (happens regularly today).
commonMistake.whyWrong: Past Participles carry the passive action meaning, while 'be' carries the tense.

checkpointData.prompt: In 'Fresh guavas are packed in bamboo baskets every morning', what role does 'Fresh guavas' play?

options.label: The Subject and the doer packing the baskets
options.explanation: Guavas cannot pack baskets—they receive the packing action.

options.label: The Subject and the receiver of the action (Passive Voice)
options.explanation: 'Fresh guavas' sits in the Subject slot and receives the present-habit action 'are packed'.

options.label: An adverbial telling when the action happens
options.explanation: 'every morning' tells when; 'Fresh guavas' is the noun Subject.

teachingSequence.title: The Object Check & 4-Step Passive Shift
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Spot the Direct Object ('Verb + what/whom?'), move it to Subject, add matching 'be' + Past Participle, and add 'by + doer' if helpful.
teachingSequence.explanation: Converting Active S + V + O to Passive follows four reliable moves. First check that the active verb actually has an Object to promote!

clausePatternData.whyItWorks: In 'The chef washes fresh vegetables', asking 'washes what?' gives 'fresh vegetables'. Moving that Object into Subject spot forces the verb to split into 'be' (tense + agreement) + 'washed' (action).
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Passive follows 4 moves: (1) Object -> New Subject, (2) matching be, (3) Past Participle (V-en), (4) optional by + doer.

relationDiagram.rightText: Fresh vegetables (New S) + are washed (be + V-en) + by the chef
relationDiagram.caption: Move the entire Object noun group together ('Fresh vegetables', not just 'vegetables').

progressiveExamples.sentence: Mira cleans the globe. -> The globe is cleaned by Mira.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Object: 'the globe'. 2) Singular present be: 'is'. 3) Participle: 'cleaned'. 4) Optional agent: 'by Mira'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Preserves Present Simple time cleanly.

progressiveExamples.sentence: The students clean the laboratory. -> The laboratory is cleaned by the students.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Active verb 'clean' matched plural 'students'. 2) New Subject 'The laboratory' is singular -> switch to 'is cleaned'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: New Subject controls 'be', even though 'students' was plural.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Volunteers pack nutritious lunch boxes daily. -> Nutritious lunch boxes are packed by volunteers daily.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Move the full Object noun phrase ('Nutritious lunch boxes') together. 2) Match plural 'are' + 'packed'. 3) Keep 'daily' at the end.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Adjectives stay attached to their noun when moving to Subject.

commonMistake.incorrectText: Fresh vegetables washed by the chef.
commonMistake.correctText: Fresh vegetables are washed by the chef.
commonMistake.whyWrong: Dropping 'be' ('are') leaves no passive verb—it makes it sound as if vegetables washed someone!

teachingSequence.title: Matching 'be' to the New Subject & Irregular V-en Forms
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Always lock 'be' onto the NEW Subject (never the old doer), and use Past Participle (V-en / V3)—never Simple Past (V2)!
teachingSequence.explanation: Two classic traps happen right after swapping Subject and Object: leaving 'be' in the old Subject's number, or grabbing Simple Past V2 ('wrote', 'ate', 'sang') instead of Past Participle V-en ('written', 'eaten', 'sung').

clausePatternData.categoryBadge: Topic 2 · Two Jobs Inside Passive Verbs
clausePatternData.whyItWorks: In 'Two science notes were written by Arjun', 'were' carries Past tense and agrees with plural 'notes' (not singular Arjun), while 'written' supplies the Past Participle V-en / V3.
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Match 'be' (is/are, was/were) to the new Subject, and lock the main verb to its Past Participle (V-en / V3).

keyTerms.meaning: Check singular vs plural on the NEW Subject: 'notes' -> were (not was); 'dosas' -> were.
Irregular forms differ from V2: wrote -> written, ate -> eaten, grew -> grown, broke -> broken, sang -> sung.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Arjun ate two ripe bananas. -> Two ripe bananas were eaten by Arjun.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) New Subject 'Two ripe bananas' is plural -> 'were'. 2) Past Participle of 'eat' is 'eaten' (never 'ate').
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Fixes both plural agreement and irregular participle.

progressiveExamples.sentence: The wind broke three clay pots. -> Three clay pots were broken by the wind.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Plural 'Three clay pots' takes 'were'. 2) Use 'broken' instead of 'broke'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Singular 'wind' disappears into 'by'; 'were' matches 'pots'.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Our choir sang the prayer song beautifully. -> The prayer song was sung beautifully by our choir.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Singular 'The prayer song' -> 'was'. 2) Participle of 'sing' is 'sung' (V3).
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Separates V2 'sang' from V3 'sung'.

commonMistake.incorrectText: The crisp dosas was served by our school canteen.
commonMistake.correctText: The crisp dosas were served by our school canteen.
commonMistake.whyWrong: 'The crisp dosas' is plural, so 'be' must shift from 'was' to 'were'.

boardNote.label: Grammar Note · V-en vs V3 Labels
boardNote.text: Different grammar guides call the third verb form 'Past Participle', 'V-en', or 'V3'. They all mean the exact same form used after 'have' and passive 'be' (written, grown, given, taken).

checkpointData.prompt: Which sentence accurately converts 'The gardener planted three neem saplings' into Passive Voice?

options.label: Three neem saplings was planted by the gardener.
options.explanation: 'Three neem saplings' is plural, so 'was' breaks Subject–Verb Agreement.

options.label: Three neem saplings planted by the gardener.
options.explanation: Missing passive 'be' makes it sound like the saplings did the planting.

options.label: Three neem saplings were planted by the gardener.
options.explanation: Plural new Subject 'Three neem saplings' takes past plural 'were' + Past Participle 'planted'.

options.label: Three neem saplings are planted by the gardener.
options.explanation: 'planted' in the original sentence is Past time, so changing to Present 'are' shifts tense.

teachingSequence.title: Simple vs Progressive ('being + V-en') Passive Chains
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: To keep an ongoing (-ing) action ongoing in Passive Voice, insert 'being' between tense 'be' and the Past Participle.
teachingSequence.explanation: Never drop ongoing meaning when shifting Voice! Compare Simple Passive ('is painted' = habit) with Progressive / Continuous Passive ('is being painted' = happening right now).

clausePatternData.whyItWorks: Active 'are painting' has two signals: Present time + ongoing (-ing). In Passive, 'is' keeps Present time (matching singular 'chart'), 'being' carries the -ing ongoing signal, and 'painted' gives the Past Participle.
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Progressive / Continuous Passive keeps ongoing meaning by inserting 'being': am/is/are/was/were + being + V-en.

keyTerms.meaning: am / is / are (Present) or was / were (Past), matched to the new Subject.
Always 'being'—shows the action is in progress at that moment.
Past Participle completing the Passive chain.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Arjun is checking the rain gauge. -> The rain gauge is being checked by Arjun.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Singular 'The rain gauge' -> 'is'. 2) Keep ongoing -ing with 'being'. 3) Add V-en 'checked'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Shows the checking is happening right now.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Workers were repairing the wooden bridge yesterday. -> The wooden bridge was being repaired yesterday.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Singular 'bridge' in Past -> 'was'. 2) Ongoing marker -> 'being'. 3) V-en -> 'repaired'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Switches plural 'were' to singular 'was' for 'bridge' while keeping 'being'.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Compare: 'Our courtyard is swept daily' (habit) vs 'Our courtyard is being swept right now' (in progress).
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Habit/routine -> no 'being' ('is swept'). 2) Happening now -> must include 'being' ('is being swept').
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Dropping 'being' erases the 'right now' meaning.

commonMistake.incorrectText: The rain gauge is checked by Arjun right now.
commonMistake.correctText: The rain gauge is being checked by Arjun right now.
commonMistake.whyWrong: Without 'being', 'is checked' sounds like a general routine rather than an action happening at this moment.

teachingSequence.title: Perfect ('been'), Future & Modal ('be') Passives
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Keep 'has/have/had' (Perfect), 'will/going to' (Future), or modals ('can/must/should') at the front, then add 'been + V-en' or 'be + V-en'.
teachingSequence.explanation: Across Perfect, Future Time, and Modal sentences, the front helper preserves the original time or attitude, while 'been' or 'be' + Past Participle adds the Passive layer.

clausePatternData.whyItWorks: After 'has / have / had', grammar requires the Past Participle 'been' before the main verb's V-en ('has been launched'). After 'will' or modals ('can, may, must, should'), grammar always requires bare 'be' ('must be worn').
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Perfect Passive uses has/have/had + been + V-en; Future & Modal Passives use will/modal + be + V-en.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Mira has prepared fresh lemon water. -> Fresh lemon water has been prepared by Mira.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Singular 'water' keeps 'has'. 2) Insert 'been'. 3) Keep Past Participle 'prepared'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Never drop 'been' after 'has/have/had'.

progressiveExamples.sentence: The principal will announce the quiz results tomorrow. -> The quiz results will be announced tomorrow.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Keep 'will'. 2) Insert base 'be'. 3) Add Past Participle 'announced'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Modals and 'will' never take 'is/are' or 'been' directly—always bare 'be'.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Students had cleaned all desks before the fair -> All desks had been cleaned before the fair.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Past Perfect 'had' stays unchanged for all subjects. 2) Insert 'been' + V-en 'cleaned'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Shows completion before another past event.

commonMistake.incorrectText: The weather satellite has launched by ISRO.
commonMistake.correctText: The weather satellite has been launched by ISRO.
commonMistake.whyWrong: Missing 'been' turns the passive verb into an active verb ('satellite launched'). Always put 'been' after has/have/had in Passive.

boardNote.label: Grammar Note · Tenses Without Standard Passives
boardNote.text: Perfect Continuous ('has been watering') and Future Continuous ('will be watering') do not normally form standard passives—stacking forms like 'has been being watered' is awkward and avoided in English.

checkpointData.prompt: Choose the accurate Passive version of 'ISRO has launched the weather satellite.'

options.label: The weather satellite was launched by ISRO.
options.explanation: Original 'has launched' is Present Perfect, not Simple Past.

options.label: The weather satellite has launched by ISRO.
options.explanation: Missing 'been' makes 'has launched' active.

options.label: The weather satellite has been launched by ISRO.
options.explanation: Keeps 'has' and inserts 'been' before Past Participle 'launched'.

options.label: The weather satellite is being launched by ISRO.
options.explanation: 'is being' shifts completed Present Perfect into ongoing Progressive.

teachingSequence.title: Pronoun Case Swaps Across the Verb
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: When pronouns cross the verb between Active and Passive, switch their case: I ↔ me, we ↔ us, he ↔ him, she ↔ her, they ↔ them, who ↔ whom.
teachingSequence.explanation: Unlike nouns ('Mira' stays 'Mira'), personal pronouns change spelling depending on whether they sit in the Subject spot or after 'by' (Object spot).

clausePatternData.categoryBadge: Topic 4 · Subject vs Object Pronoun Case
clausePatternData.whyItWorks: Any preposition—including 'by'—requires an Object-case pronoun (me, us, him, her, them, whom). And any pronoun moving into the Subject slot requires Subject case (I, we, he, she, they, who).
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Swap pronoun case on both sides: Subject (I, we, he, she, they, who) <-> by + Object (me, us, him, her, them, whom).

keyTerms.meaning: I, we, you, he, she, it, they, who (sit in the Subject slot before the verb).
me, us, you, him, her, it, them, whom (sit after 'by' or an active verb).

segments.label: Subject Case
segments.text: I · we · he · she · they · who

segments.label: by + Object Case
segments.text: me · us · him · her · them · whom

relationDiagram.caption: Both pronouns flip form when trading Subject and Object positions.

progressiveExamples.sentence: He helps us. -> We are helped by him.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) 'us' becomes Subject 'We'. 2) Plural 'We' takes 'are helped'. 3) 'He' becomes 'by him'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Both Subject and Object cases match their new slots.

progressiveExamples.sentence: They invited me to the science fair. -> I was invited to the science fair by them.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) 'me' moves to Subject 'I'. 2) Singular 'I' takes Past 'was invited'. 3) 'They' moves to 'by them'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Matches 'I was' and 'by them'.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Who planted this banyan tree? -> By whom was this banyan tree planted?
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) After 'By', 'Who' changes to Object case 'whom'. 2) Invert 'was' before 'this banyan tree'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Conversational English also allows 'Who was this banyan tree planted by?'

commonMistake.incorrectText: The kite was flown by he.
commonMistake.correctText: The kite was flown by him.
commonMistake.whyWrong: 'by' is a preposition, so it must take Object case 'him', never Subject case 'he'.

teachingSequence.title: Two Objects (SVOO), Questions & Imperatives
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Verbs with two Objects allow two passives; Questions put 'be' before the Subject (never 'did'); Commands use 'Let + Object + be + V-en'.
teachingSequence.explanation: Once you know the core 4-step shift, three special patterns—Double-Object (SVOO), Interrogative Questions, and Imperative instructions—follow clean word-order rules.

clausePatternData.whyItWorks: SVOO clauses have both a recipient (IO) and a thing (DO), so either can step into Subject position. Questions move only the first auxiliary in front of the new Subject and drop 'do/does/did'.
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Promote IO (or DO + to/for) for SVOO; replace do/does/did with inverted be in Questions; use Let + O + be + V-en for Commands.

segments.label: SVOO Option B
segments.text: A certificate was given to Mira.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Water the saplings daily. -> Let the saplings be watered daily.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Start with 'Let'. 2) Place Object 'the saplings'. 3) Finish with 'be' + V-en 'watered'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Advice/rules can also use 'The saplings should be watered daily'; polite requests use 'You are requested to...'.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Did Mira bring the globe? -> Was the globe brought by Mira?
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Drop 'Did'. 2) Place Past singular 'Was' at the start before 'the globe'. 3) Use V-en 'brought'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Never leave 'do, does, did' in a Passive question.

progressiveExamples.sentence: The librarian lent our class three atlases. -> Three atlases were lent to our class by the librarian.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Promote Direct Object 'Three atlases' -> plural 'were lent'. 2) Insert 'to' before 'our class'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Dropping 'to' ('lent our class' after 'Three atlases') sounds incomplete in this order.

commonMistake.incorrectText: Did the courtyard cleaned by the students?
commonMistake.correctText: Was the courtyard cleaned by the students?
commonMistake.whyWrong: Passive questions replace 'did / do / does' with a form of 'be' ('was / were / is / are').

checkpointData.prompt: Which is the accurate Passive form of 'Who planted this banyan tree?'

options.label: By who was this banyan tree planted?
options.explanation: After preposition 'By', 'who' must change to Object case 'whom'.

options.label: By whom was this banyan tree planted?
options.explanation: Uses Object case 'whom' after 'By' and places 'was' before the new Subject 'this banyan tree'.

options.label: By whom this banyan tree planted?
options.explanation: Missing auxiliary 'was' and question inversion before the Subject.

teachingSequence.title: Omitting Vague 'by + Doer' & Natural Passive ('by' vs 'with')
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Drop 'by + doer' when the doer is unknown, obvious, or general ('someone, people, they'). Keep 'by' for real agents and use 'with' for tools!
teachingSequence.explanation: Real-world Passive Voice rarely adds '...by someone' or '...by people'. Science notes, heritage facts, and lost-and-found notices omit empty agents—and remember that tools use 'with', not 'by'.

clausePatternData.whyItWorks: In 'Someone swept the library steps', 'someone' adds zero new information. Dropping 'by someone' highlights the clean steps directly. By contrast, keeping 'by C.V. Raman' or 'with a clean knife' adds crucial facts.
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Omit vague 'by someone / by people'; keep informative 'by + creator'; use 'with' for physical tools.

keyTerms.meaning: Drop 'by someone / by people / by them / by everybody' and obvious police/builders agents.
Keep 'by + doer' when naming the person/organisation adds vital facts ('by ISRO', 'by C.V. Raman').
Use 'by' for people/doers and 'with' for instruments ('sliced with a clean knife').

segments.label: Omit Vague Doer
segments.text: The steps were swept before dawn.

segments.label: Keep Key Doer
segments.text: The lens was tested by C.V. Raman.

progressiveExamples.sentence: People grow spices in Kerala. -> Spices are grown in Kerala.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) 'People' is general and obvious. 2) Omit 'by people' for natural geography writing.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Adding '...by people' sounds repetitive and clunky.

progressiveExamples.sentence: The Konark Sun Temple was built in the thirteenth century.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Focus stays on the monument ('The Konark Sun Temple'). 2) Past Passive 'was built' avoids filler words.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Passive is the natural voice for history and science processes.

progressiveExamples.sentence: The wood was carved with a sharp chisel by the master artisan.
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Tool: 'with a sharp chisel'. 2) Human agent: 'by the master artisan'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Distinguishes instrument from human doer cleanly.

commonMistake.incorrectText: The ripe mangoes were sliced by a clean knife.
commonMistake.correctText: The ripe mangoes were sliced with a clean knife.
commonMistake.whyWrong: A knife is a physical tool, not a person—tools take 'with', whereas doers take 'by'.

checkpointData.prompt: Which Passive sentence sounds most natural for 'Someone has returned the missing science book'?

options.label: The missing science book has been returned by someone.
options.explanation: 'by someone' adds no information and should be dropped.

options.label: The missing science book has returned.
options.explanation: Missing 'been' turns the verb active—a book cannot return itself!

options.label: The missing science book has been returned.
options.explanation: Preserves Present Perfect Passive ('has been returned') and cleanly omits vague 'by someone'.

teachingSequence.title: Sentences That Cannot Be Made Passive
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Only verbs with a real Object (SVO, SVOO, SVOC) can become Passive! Intransitive (SV/SVA) and Linking (SVC) verbs have no Object to promote.
teachingSequence.explanation: Before trying to convert a sentence, run the Object Test ('Verb + what or whom?'). Place/time phrases, Subject Complements, and '-ed' feeling adjectives are NOT Passive!

clausePatternData.whyItWorks: Passive Voice moves an Object into the Subject slot. If a verb is intransitive ('arrived at six', 'slept soundly') or linking ('felt cool', 'became captain'), there is zero Object to move.
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Intransitive (SV, SVA) and Linking (SVC) clauses lack an Object and cannot form Passive Voice.

keyTerms.meaning: Action has no receiver Object ('arrived at six' tells when, not what).
Describes the Subject ('breeze = cool and fresh'), not a separate Object.
'were excited / was tired' describes feeling (test with 'very excited')—not a Passive action!

progressiveExamples.sentence: The baby slept peacefully. (SVA -> No Passive)
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Ask 'slept what?' -> No answer! 2) 'peacefully' tells how (Adverbial), not an Object.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Cannot be turned into Passive.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Priya became the school captain. (SVC -> No Passive)
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) 'the school captain' = 'Priya' (Complement). 2) Nobody acted on a separate object.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: 'The school captain was become by Priya' is ungrammatical.

progressiveExamples.sentence: The students were interested in astronomy. (be + Adjective, NOT Passive)
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Try putting 'very' before it -> 'very interested' works! 2) True passive actions like 'caught' fail 'very caught'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: 'interested' describes a state of mind, not an action done by an agent.

commonMistake.incorrectText: Trying to convert 'Arjun sat on the wooden bench' -> 'The wooden bench was sat on by Arjun'.
commonMistake.correctText: Leave simple Intransitive SVA sentences in Active Voice ('Arjun sat on the wooden bench').
commonMistake.whyWrong: 'sat' is intransitive and 'on the wooden bench' is a place adverbial, not a Direct Object.

checkpointData.prompt: Which sentence CANNOT be changed into Passive Voice?

options.label: The eco-club planted fifty bamboo saplings.
options.explanation: 'fifty bamboo saplings' is a Direct Object -> 'Fifty bamboo saplings were planted...'

options.label: Warm sunlight filled the courtyard.
options.explanation: 'the courtyard' is a Direct Object -> 'The courtyard was filled with warm sunlight.'

options.label: The morning breeze felt cool and fresh.
options.explanation: 'felt' is a linking verb followed by adjectives ('cool and fresh' describing the breeze). Without an Object, no Passive exists.

teachingSequence.title: Spotting & Fixing Voice Errors (5-Point Check)
teachingSequence.shortPrompt: Before finishing any Passive sentence, run the 5-Point Voice Check: Object, Pronoun Case, 'be' Match, V-en Form, and Concise 'by'.
teachingSequence.explanation: Most Active-Passive slips happen when one detail changes (like moving a plural Object to Subject) and the rest of the sentence forgets to update.

clausePatternData.whyItWorks: Checking each of the 5 links separately—(1) Object exists, (2) Pronoun case matches slot, (3) 'be' carries exact tense + new-Subject agreement, (4) main verb is Past Participle V-en, (5) vague 'by someone' dropped—catches every hidden slip.
clausePatternData.ruleSummary: Check Object -> Pronoun case -> 'be' (tense + new Subject) -> Past Participle (V-en) -> Omit vague 'by'.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Broken: 'A new library has built near our school.' -> Fixed: 'A new library has been built near our school.'
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) A library cannot build itself (Passive needed). 2) Insert 'been' between 'has' and 'built'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Completes the Present Perfect Passive chain.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Broken: 'Did the broken bench repaired yesterday?' -> Fixed: 'Was the broken bench repaired yesterday?'
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Passive questions never use 'Did'. 2) Replace 'Did' with singular past 'Was' before 'the broken bench'.
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Restores proper passive question inversion.

progressiveExamples.sentence: Broken: 'The science posters was drew by they.' -> Fixed: 'The science posters were drawn by them.'
progressiveExamples.stepByStep: 1) Plural 'posters' -> 'were' (not 'was'). 2) Past Participle -> 'drawn' (not V2 'drew'). 3) After 'by' -> Object pronoun 'them' (not 'they').
progressiveExamples.whyCorrect: Fixes agreement, participle, and pronoun case together.

commonMistake.incorrectText: The fresh vegetables is being washed by she before lunch.
commonMistake.correctText: The fresh vegetables are being washed by her before lunch.
commonMistake.whyWrong: Plural Subject 'vegetables' needs 'are', and object position after 'by' needs 'her'.

checkpointData.prompt: Find the errors in: 'The fresh vegetables is being washed by she before lunch.'

options.label: Missing 'been' after 'is'
options.explanation: 'being' is accurate for ongoing action; the errors are agreement and pronoun case.

options.label: 'is' should be 'are' (plural 'vegetables') and 'she' should be 'her'
options.explanation: Plural Subject 'The fresh vegetables' takes 'are being washed', and 'by' requires Object case 'her'.

options.label: 'washed' should be 'wash'
options.explanation: Passive verbs always end in Past Participle 'washed', never base 'wash'.
